correctness.rationale: Starting from Gnedin–Olshanski exact two-index displacement mass, weighted double sum is absolutely dominated in q<|z|<1/q by two convergent geometric series. Two standard q-binomial summations, using (1−q)(q²;q)∞=(q;q)∞, give PGF (q;q)∞²/[(qz;q)∞(q/z;q)∞]. Each factor is a geometric-variable PGF; finite total expectations imply almost-sure convergence of two sums and uniqueness of Laurent coefficients. At z=−1, product ∏((1−q^j)/(1+q^j))² is strictly positive and <1; termwise factor comparison, strict at j=1 and absolute log convergence, makes it strictly decrease with q. The previously known identification of fixed-point means with parity at q=1/Q completes c_o(Q)>1/2>c_e(Q), strict monotonicities. This analytic proof justifies all Q>1; rational finite truncation checker only corroborates.
